key_insight: Cryogenic terahertz nanoscopy can spatially resolve the bulk photovoltaic effect in bilayer graphene, directly linking quantum geometry and nonlinear photoresponse.
engineering_relevance: This enables a new optical diagnostic for optimizing quantum-material-based photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices by separating intrinsic BPVE from contact and thermoelectric artifacts.
method: Dual-gated AB bilayer graphene measured with polarization-sensitive terahertz microscopy
Deep-subwavelength cryogenic imaging to map local photoresponse
Carrier-density and temperature sweeps to isolate symmetry- and geometry-driven signals
evidence_signal: The abstract reports enhanced optical conductivity and spatially resolved BPVE near band-gap/terahertz resonance, with polarization-dependent twofold symmetry and agreement with theory.
watch_item: The technique is cryogenic and material-specific, so translating it to practical devices may require careful control of temperature, gating, and interface effects.
paper_title: Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene
